source_prompt:
# Instructions for accurately documenting a failed industrial safety audit

1. Start with the inspection records.
2.
completion:
Obtain and review all existing inspection records related to the site/facility to derive a baseline understanding of the safety performance and prior identified issues. 

3. List the failed sections.
Detail all sections of the audit that the facility failed to meet compliance, referencing specific safety standards, codes, and regulations. 

4. Document specific violations.
Provide a detailed account of each non-conformity or violation found during the audit, including time, location, and nature of the violation as well as any potential consequences if left unaddressed.

5. Include photos or videos (if available and permissible).
Where applicable, use visual documentation to substantiate the violations found, ensuring that such evidence is dated, timestamped, and clearly labeled. Make sure you have permission to include any photos or videos in your report.

6. Identify the root cause.
Analyze and describe the underlying reasons behind each failure. This might include lack of proper training, insufficient supervision, outdated procedures
